# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** She extends her power from one end of the universe to the other, and brings all things into beautiful order.

**8:2** I fell in love with her from my earliest years. I wanted to make her my bride, and her beauty filled me with longing.

**8:3** Her nobility shines through her closeness with God — the Lord of all things chose to love her.

**8:4** She is the one admitted into God's own knowledge, the one he invites to choose alongside him in all his works.

**8:5** If wealth is something worth wanting in this life, nothing is richer than Wisdom — she who brings everything into being.

**8:6** If skill and understanding matter, who in all the world is a greater master craftsman than she?

**8:7** And if virtue is what you are after, her labors produce exactly that: she teaches self-control and discernment, justice and courage — and nothing in human life is more valuable than these four.

**8:8** If wide experience is your desire, she knows the past and foresees the future; she sees through the turns of clever speech, she can unlock any riddle; she has advance knowledge of signs and wonders, and she knows how the seasons and ages will unfold.

**8:9** So I made up my mind to bring her home as my companion, knowing she would be a guide to what is good — and on hard days, a comfort.

**8:10** Because of her, I would be honored among crowds and respected by the elders, young as I am.

**8:11** I would prove myself sharp when judgment is needed, and the sight of rulers would inspire wonder in them.

**8:12** When I kept silent, they would wait; when I spoke, they would lean in; when I held the floor longer, they would cover their mouths in respectful attention.

**8:13** Through her, I would lay hold of immortality — and leave behind a memory that would endure for all who come after me.

**8:14** I would govern peoples, and nations would fall under my rule.

**8:15** Even the most formidable rulers, hearing my name, would be afraid; in the company of the crowd I would be seen as good, and in battle I would show courage.

**8:16** Coming home at the end of the day, I would rest beside her — for there is nothing bitter about her company, and life shared with her brings no grief, only happiness and delight.

**8:17** Turning all this over in my mind — that immortality comes through kinship with Wisdom,

**8:18** that her friendship is pure pleasure, that her hands hold inexhaustible wealth, that living closely with her deepens understanding, that speaking with her brings great renown — I set out to find a way to make her mine.

**8:19** I was a naturally gifted child, and I was blessed with a good soul.

**8:20** Better still: because I was good, I entered the world in a body that was pure and undefiled.

**8:21** But I knew I could not truly master myself without God's help — and even seeing that was itself a kind of wisdom, knowing from whom the gift must come. So I turned to the Lord and made my appeal; I prayed with my whole heart:
